system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:43, WS-ICHEN-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01; at 13:45, sam.okafor launched PowerShell to run the inventory-listed Apply-Updates.ps1 script from FILE-NWD-01.

The PowerShell process initiated a proxy connection to download.windowsupdate.com, and its child wusa.exe installed a Windows update package. This is consistent with the documented patching practice and scheduled workstation patching, but does not by itself establish that this was the window ivy.chen reported.
The provided records show no PowerShell process creation around 13:40; the recorded PowerShell process creation is at 13:45.

At 14:16, a Sysmon registry event recorded ivy.chen's UserAssist entry for powershell.exe. This supports PowerShell usage being recorded for her profile, but does not establish when it was launched or whether it relates to the reported window.

The workstation connected to desktop.dropbox.com with a DropboxUpdate user agent, and DropboxUpdate.exe was later observed running. Dropbox is not among the services listed as approved in the supplied inventory; these records do not establish malicious use.

GoogleDriveFS.exe was launched under ivy.chen's account. Google Drive is not among the services listed as approved in the supplied inventory; the launch alone does not establish malicious use or data transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include the contents, hash, or execution results of Apply-Updates.ps1.
The records show process creation and network metadata, but do not establish what was visible on ivy.chen's screen or whether the reported window was interactive.
The UserAssist event records a PowerShell path but does not establish the launch time or link it to the reported observation.
The Dropbox and Google Drive records do not show what data, if any, was uploaded or downloaded.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported PowerShell window was the authorized patching activity at 13:45 or a separate PowerShell launch.
Whether the Dropbox and Google Drive software or activity was authorized by an exception, and whether either service was used to transfer organizational data.
Whether any malicious command, payload, or other harmful action occurred.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with sam.okafor and the patch/change records whether the 13:43 remote logon and 13:45 patch run were authorized and whether they explain the reported window.
Collect the script contents and hash, relevant PowerShell operational logs, and fuller endpoint process and interactive-session telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01.
Verify the installation and authorization status of Dropbox and Google Drive, and review their file-access and transfer history for the relevant period.
